title: Webinar: Unpacking public action for information integrity on climate and the environment
content:
A few days before COP31 kicks off in Antalya, Türkiye, the Forum on Information and Democracy will bring together international experts and policymakers for an online webinar on public policies to strengthen information integrity on climate and the environment.

Climate disinformation, denial and greenwashing continue to undermine public understanding and slow progress towards the ecological transition. How can governments respond? What policies are already being implemented around the world, and what lessons can be drawn from these experiences?

Published on 13 October, the Forum’s new report, Mapping International Policy and Regulatory Frameworks for Climate and Environmental Information Integrity, offers the first international mapping of government efforts to address these challenges. Covering 23 countries and the European Union, it provides a practical resource for governments, civil society organizations, journalists and all stakeholders working to protect the integrity of public debate on climate and the environment.

title: Third meeting: Information integrity in the age of AI, from manipulation to regulatory responses
content:
The Workstream on Safeguarding Access to Reliable Information in the Age of AI held its third meeting on 1 October 2026. Co-chaired by Luxembourg, Spain and Ukraine, the closed-door online session brought together representatives of signatory States of the Partnership for Information and Democracy, civil society and researchers. The discussion focused on information integrity and manipulation: the technical challenges identified, the open questions for research, regulatory gaps and the policy responses emerging across regions.

Key insights from researchers, government and regulatory authorities

How AI is changing manipulation

The first half of the meeting focused on the issues at stake, looking at how AI also affects and distorts the flow of information itself through algorithmic gatekeeping, influence operations, and manipulation. It is increasingly used to sow distrust, to emphasize some views for political gain, or, as some speakers emphasized for economic gain.

title: Climate disinformation: new report confirms that political will is there, but actions remain limited at national level
content:
A new report from the Forum on Information and Democracy (FID) finds notable political will and promising efforts to strengthen information integrity on climate change in at least 23 countries and the EU. However, it also finds persistent gaps, such as lack of national strategic plans of action to tackle climate disinformation and greenwashing from the fossil fuel lobby, which is most urgently needed.

As the world prepares for COP 17 on Biodiversity (22-30 October) and COP31 on climate change (9-22 November), the findings pave the way for policymakers and regulators to take the urgent action needed to tackle climate disinformation. 

Covering 23 countries and the EU, the report was developed within the framework of the organization’s priority workstream on Information Integrity on Climate and the Environment, co-chaired by Armenia and Brazil.  It shows that while political traction and public awareness are rising, most countries still don’t have a national strategic plan of action to counter climate disinformation and denialism.

title: New video makes the economic case for investing in public interest media to mark World News Day
content:
Disinformation continues to represent a top global threat and with AI further harming access to reliable information while eroding the visibility, and by extension, the viability of quality journalism. As stated by the High Level Panel on Public Interest media a year ago,  it is more urgent than ever to recognise the social and economic value of public interest media and properly invest in it like the public good it is. 

Paris, 25 September 2026. Ahead of World News Day on 28 September, the Forum on Information and Democracy (FID), in partnership with the International Fund for Public Interest Media (IFPIM), has released a short video renewing the call for governments and policymakers to invest in public interest media.

One year ago, the High-Level Panel on Public Interest Media, which was convened by FID and comprising 11 leading economists, including three Nobel Prizes, published a landmark statement making the economic case for such investment. The statement was picked up by over 80 media outlets and helped shape World News Day‘s call to action.

title: Mapping policy frameworks for climate information integrity – 8th meeting of workstream on information integrity on climate change and the environment
content:
Many governments signed the Belém Declaration on Information Integrity on Climate Change. Comprehensive strategies to implement it are still lacking, but inspiring practices are conducted by policy makers in several countries as discussed during the workstream meeting. It was the occasion to present the preliminary results of the first mapping exercise of its kind covering 23 countries and the EU.

On 16 September 2026, the Forum on Information and Democracy held the eighth overall and the third annual meeting of the Workstream on Information Integrity on Climate Change & Other Environmental Issues, co-chaired by Brazil and Armenia. 

This meeting offered insights about the FID’s mapping exercise to assess countries’ regulatory and policy frameworks to promote climate and environmental information integrity. It also enabled a deep dive into specific countries’ practices notably by Poland, Canada and France as well as civil society efforts regarding advertising transparency.

title: Call for Contributions: Newsfluencers and Public Interest Media
content:
The Forum on Information and Democracy (FID) is preparing an insight report examining the relationship between news content creators (or so called “newsfluencers”) and public interest journalism and welcomes contributions from experts.

The report will look at how the creator economy is reshaping the information ecosystem: the competitive and financial pressures it places on traditional media, the spectrum of actors – from independent journalists to entertainment-driven influencers, the strategies newsrooms are adopting to compete or collaborate with creators, and the policy frameworks that could help news content creators become allies of information integrity.

We welcome contributions from researchers, journalists, media organizations, platforms, policymakers, and content creators themselves, including:

  • Reports, studies, or data on the creator economy’s impact on news media business models and audience behavior
  • Analysis or case studies on news content creators’ editorial practices, self-regulation, or professional norms
  • Examples of media-creator partnerships, transformation strategies, or creator studios

title: How to mobilise the Open Government Partnership to promote information integrity in Francophone Africa
content:
In spring 2026, the Open Government Partnership (OGP) commissioned FID to work with Benin, Ivory Coast, Morocco and Senegal to incorporate the issues of information integrity and press freedom into their national action plans. In its report, FID provides an overview of the issues and presents recommendations for the four countries.

Access to reliable information is a cornerstone of open government. Yet, this right is threatened by the current changes of the information space, in particular digital platforms, the development and deployment of generative artificial intelligence, the mass dissemination of disinformation, and the fragility of the business model of independent media.

Building upon these observations the Open Government Partnership (OGP) commissioned FID to carry out a project between February 2026 and June 2026 in Benin, Ivory Coast, Morocco and Senegal. The aim was to ensure that issues relating to press freedom and information integrity were given greater consideration in the co-creation processes for the OGP’s national action plans.

title: Second Meeting: How AI is harming public interest media’s sustainability? First findings from FID’s dedicated workstream
content:
As Artificial Intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping our information ecosystems, public interest media faces historical challenges regarding its sustainability. Facilitated by the Forum on Information and Democracy and led by Luxembourg, Spain and Ukraine, the Workstream on Safeguarding Access to Reliable Information in the Age of AI held its second meeting highlighting this specific challenge and possible policy responses. 

On 18 June 2026, the Forum on Information and Democracy held the second meeting of its workstream on Safeguarding access to reliable information in the age of AI. On this occasion, María González Veracruz, Secretary of State for Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence of Spain, announced that the country was joining Luxembourg and Ukraine in the co-chairship of the workstream. As she noted,

“False content is easy to spread and difficult to disprove…international cooperation is essential for the overarching goal of protecting information integrity, trust, and democracy.”

title: New challenges and approaches in the fight against Climate Disinformation – insights from the workstream on information integrity on climate change and the environment
content:
Climate disinformation is not only employed to delay climate action, but is interconnected with other goals, such as foreign interference, as the conversations of the workstream highlight. This requires that governments think of comprehensive approaches to tackle the problem.  Parliamentary inquiries and recommendations as well as  new communications campaigns can play a role to protect the information space and ensure democratic debates.

On 3rd June 2026, the Forum on Information and Democracy held the seventh overall and the second annual meeting of the Workstream on Information Integrity on Climate Change & Other Environmental Issues, co-chaired by Brazil and Armenia. 

This meeting offered evidence about the nexus between climate disinformation and Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI), a topic currently underresearched. It also provided insights into specific initiatives to promote information integrity such as parliamentary inquiries and communication approaches. In the run-up to the COP17 to be held in October 2026, the Forum will also release its interim report of the workstream, whose structure was presented.

title: First Meeting of the Workstream on Artificial Intelligence highlights the comprehensive challenges and new trends regarding reliable information
content:
The first meeting of this workstream was held on 29 April, 2026. It gathered representatives of signatory States of the Partnership as well as civil society experts and researchers. The meeting involved expounding the current economic challenges to the information ecosystem in the face of AI. It also considered the existential threats to media sustainability, and what a weakened media ecosystem does to public trust and knowledge. Finally, the meeting briefly touched upon global regulatory approaches, and started discussions on possible policy interventions.

This first meeting revealed the multitude of challenges faced in the realm of AI and the information space globally.
